name: Local AI and Mission Control
tagline: A private, local-first AI assistant with a model router, a web control panel and voice.
overview: A self-hosted AI assistant that runs open-weight language models on a home GPU and only reaches out to cloud models when a request is eligible and the owner allows it. An agent layer keeps projects, chats and tasks organized, and a router decides which model may handle each request. Mission Control is the everyday web interface, designed to feel as simple as a mainstream chat app while keeping operator tools on a separate admin page.
features: Local-first routing: ordinary questions stay on a local model; cloud use needs explicit approval, spending caps and sensitivity checks
Mission Control web UI with Chat, Apps, Devices, Services and Import pages, installable on a phone as a web app
Voice conversation using local speech recognition and text-to-speech
Approval-gated actions: the assistant proposes changes and the owner confirms each one
Manages a small fleet of home-lab machines and containers, with read-only access by default
Self-hosted push notifications planned for a native Android app

name: AI Phone Control
tagline: Voice-triggered Android automations with a monitor that checks whether they actually worked.
overview: A dedicated Android phone runs automation workflows that operate other apps on request, triggered by smart-speaker voice commands through a home automation hub. Because tapping through another app's UI can fail silently, a companion monitor watches each run, captures the screen state and classifies the outcome instead of trusting a simple success code. The project repaired and hardened an earlier set of workflows and added health checks so problems are noticed quickly.
features: Phone workflows wake the screen, read the target app's UI and act only when the expected state is present
Voice commands via a smart speaker and a home automation hub, plus a custom integration and skill
Node.js monitor that follows each run and sorts results into clear outcomes (failed, blocked, already on, confirmed, unconfirmed)
On-device text recognition fallback when animations prevent reading the UI tree
Heartbeat and watchdog alerts if the phone goes quiet or a scheduled run cannot be confirmed
Deliberately no blind retries after an uncertain result

name: ChampLeague
tagline: A fast 3v3 arcade football (soccer) game prototype built in Roblox Studio.
overview: An original arcade football game where each human player controls a single footballer in quick three-a-side matches, with automated goalkeepers and a server-authoritative ball. It is a family-friendly hobby project: contributors suggest ideas in plain language through a GitHub issue form, and changes are reviewed and playtested in Roblox Studio before they are merged. The current build is a Studio-only prototype on the way to a small first release.
features: 3v3 matches with up to six human players, spectating and AI goalkeepers
Pass, charged shot, juke, tackle, sprint and stamina, with simple player ratings
Keyboard and mouse, controller and touch controls
Cosmetic move styles that never change gameplay balance
Selectable team kit palettes and a roster screen
Plain-language request workflow using GitHub issues and reviewed pull requests

name: Family Hub
tagline: Turns emailed invitations into reviewable calendar proposals for a shared family calendar.
overview: A small desktop helper connected to a dedicated email account and a shared calendar. It scans recent mail for calendar attachments and invitation-like messages, compares them with what is already on the calendar, and produces a local review page of proposed additions, duplicates and items that need a human decision. Nothing is added automatically; the current version only reads mail and calendar data.
features: Detects calendar attachments, invitation wording and dated activity emails
Groups proposals into new events, existing events, cancellations, ambiguous items and possible duplicates
Read-only by design: it never sends email or edits events
Generates an offline HTML review page on demand
Credentials encrypted per user on the local machine and kept out of the repository
Planned: free-form email and voice requests that still require approval before anything is added

name: Camera Scan Station
tagline: Turning ordinary photos into 3D-printable STL models, no laser scanner needed.
overview: The goal is to go from a physical object to a printable STL file using only an off-the-shelf compact camera instead of an expensive laser scanner. Capture tools coordinate the camera (running custom firmware), a motorized turntable and two LED light bars to photograph the object from evenly spaced angles; photogrammetry then rebuilds those photos into a 3D mesh. Each session records its settings, and finished scans are audited and packaged with checksums for transfer to the reconstruction machine. A 12-view lighting and rotation test has succeeded; reconstruction quality is the next thing to validate.
features: Photo-to-STL pipeline: photograph an object, reconstruct a mesh with photogrammetry, export an STL
Automatic rings of photos at set angles, waiting for the turntable to settle before each shot
Saved presets for zoom, focus, ISO, aperture, shutter speed and lighting
Session metadata and camera logs recorded alongside the images
Audit tool checks image headers, dimensions, duplicates and inventory
Packaging and verification with SHA-256 checksums for safe transfer

name: Go2 Home Console
tagline: A local dashboard, voice companion and onboard-compute plan for a quadruped robot.
overview: A home console for a consumer quadruped robot that adds local camera questions, offline speech recognition, a spoken robot voice and supervised controls. The long-term goal is fully self-contained operation from a battery-powered backpack computer on the robot, so a native install on a small NVIDIA Jetson board is being built and measured alongside the desktop version. The project keeps a detailed decision history and a separate current-best-practice guide so every claim is backed by recorded evidence.
features: Browser dashboard for camera answers, speech, light commands and supervised shutdown preparation
Offline English speech recognition and local text-to-speech, with GPU acceleration where available
Phone conversation companion kept separate from robot controls
Native edge-computer build with GPU recognition and a small local chat model
Follow-me behaviour developed in an offline simulation before any real-world motion
Backpack power and mount research, including 3D-printed parts

name: Office TV Cleanup and Launcher
tagline: Stripping the ads and tracking out of a Google TV, reversibly, plus a clean custom home screen.
overview: Smart TVs ship with home screens full of ads, sponsored rows and background tracking. This project removes them: scripts turn off the preinstalled ad, promotion and telemetry packages on an Android-based Google TV without uninstalling anything, so every change can be undone. It also replaces the ad-filled home screen with a lightweight custom launcher showing a clock, weather and an editable app grid, plus a screensaver of openly licensed photos with credits.
features: Removes home-screen ads, sponsored content and usage tracking by disabling those packages; nothing is uninstalled and everything is reversible
Tiered debloat script (ads, telemetry or all) and a matching restore script
Custom launcher: clock, date, weather, app grid with move and hide, and quick buttons
Screensaver slideshow of openly licensed photos with photographer and license credits
On-TV help screen explaining how to use the launcher
Documents which system packages were left alone on purpose and why

name: Simple TV Launcher
tagline: A big-button streaming launcher for Fire TV, designed for an older family member.
overview: A planned native app for a Fire TV streaming stick that shows exactly five large, high-contrast buttons for the streaming services a relative uses most, with live TV first and focused by default. The goal is to make getting back to familiar apps easy for someone who finds standard TV menus confusing. It works within the platform's rules: it is a normal app with no root access or launcher replacement. The requirements and design are written up; implementation is starting.
features: Exactly five large, clearly labelled buttons with no scrolling, ads or extra menus
Clear remote-control focus that resets to the first button whenever the app reopens
Back on the main screen never exits by accident
Graceful message when an app is missing or fails to launch
Plain-English installation guide written for family members
Planned CI build that produces an installable package
